Answer: D
Reason: The initial chest X-ray shows diffuse, patchy bilateral alveolar infiltrates that resolve completely in the follow-up images (Figures 4a and 4b), a pattern characteristic of the rapid clearance of blood seen in recovery from exercise-induced pulmonary haemorrhage (EIPH). Other options like bacterial pneumonia or ARDS typically leave residual changes or resolve more slowly, while cardiogenic edema would likely show cardiomegaly which is not prominent here.
